question: Does a caption-only VoiceDesign voice stay one speaker across separate invocations?
why_it_matters: Speaker B fills one channel of every V-real and V-tts dialogue. If the voice differs between utterances, channel B is not a speaker but a crowd, and both voice control runs are invalid in a way no loss curve would reveal.

method.caption: 落ち着いた男性の声で、標準的な話し方で自然に読み上げてください。
method.preparation: tools.speaker_similarity: voiced frames at RMS>=500 over 480-sample windows, then RMS normalisation to 0.05
method.statistic: within-group pairwise cosine similarity over all clip pairs

calibration.note: A within-group number means nothing without knowing what one speaker scores under this exact pipeline. These bands come from the M2 audio, measured the same way.
calibration.interpretation: One speaker scores 0.70 or above when the rendering is held constant, and 0.60 across renderings. Different speakers score below 0.30. A real human is the floor at 0.698 mean / 0.565 min, because a person varies delivery between sentences more than a TTS does.

caption_only_random_seed.flags: --no-ref --caption (seed omitted, so infer.py draws a random seed per request)

caption_only_fixed_seed.verdict: not one speaker; pinning the seed does not fix the voice

frozen_reference.flags: one clip generated from the caption, then reused as --ref-wav for every other utterance
frozen_reference.verdict: one speaker; above the real-human band on both mean and minimum

conclusion.decision: Generate exactly one speaker-B clip from the caption, archive it, and pass it as --ref-wav for every speaker-B utterance in V-real and V-tts.
conclusion.rejected: Calling --no-ref --caption per utterance, with or without a fixed seed. At 0.45-0.52 it sits below the 0.565 minimum that one real human produces, which is the signature of a family of similar-but-distinct voices rather than a single speaker.
conclusion.seed_finding: --seed defaults to a fresh random seed per request (infer.py). Pinning it lifted the mean only from 0.4525 to 0.5176, still under the floor, so the drift is in the caption-only speaker sampling itself and not in the sampler seed.
conclusion.separation_confirmed: The frozen B scores 0.157 against tsukuyomi natural audio and 0.139 against the M2 TTS, so A and B are unambiguously different speakers.
conclusion.gate_for_m3: Before either dataset is tokenised, measure within-group pairwise similarity over a sample of the generated speaker-B utterances. Require mean >= 0.65 and minimum >= 0.55, the band one real human occupies. Also require mean similarity against speaker A below 0.30.
